description:
Items defined in `domain/types.rs` are imported both through the `domain` facade and through `domain::types::`, and the facade's glob re-export is justified as backward compatibility.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/domain/mod.rs:44-45` re-exports `types::*` "for backward compatibility". About 546 references in 128 files use the facade (`domain::X`). There are 339 `domain::types::` lines in 36 files. Of those, 333 are `crate::domain::types::fixture_issue`, a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` fixture (`domain/types.rs:491-492`). The other six are `domain/projection.rs:47,216`, `commands/worktree.rs:751`, `domain/store_divergence.rs:167` and two rustdoc lines in `validation/graph.rs:87-88`. Inside `domain/`, two `super::types` references remain.

A glob `pub use` re-exports `pub(crate)` items at `pub(crate)` visibility, so `crate::domain::fixture_issue` resolves in test builds. Once `mod types` is private, the compiler rejects any second path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `domain::types` is a private module, and every item defined in `domain/types.rs` is reached as `domain::<Item>`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No source, test or rustdoc path names `domain::types::`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `domain/mod.rs` carries no backward-compatibility justification for a re-export.

## Notes

The change is mechanical, with zero semantic change, and can be re-run after a rebase. The footprint lists the 39 files that name the path, measured by search at planning time; a file that gains such a path later is rewritten the same way.
title: Import domain type items through the domain facade
